Subject: Finova — Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (post-call recap)

Hi Samira / Lucas — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call plus next steps so we stay aligned.

Key takeaways (what we heard):
- Primary latency goal: P95 end-to-end response for user-facing token generation <= 200ms for US/EU regions; APAC can be relaxed to P95 <= 250ms for the initial rollout.
- Throughput & concurrency: expecting burst concurrency up to ~120 simultaneous requests per region with steady-state throughput ~600 req/min for the chat endpoint.
- Streaming: you need chunked/streaming responses (SSE or chunked transfer) for progressive rendering on web/mobile.
- Regional routing: Traffic should route to the nearest region (US / EU / APAC). EU customer data must remain in EU for residency/compliance (no cross-border dev copies).
- Fallback/backoff: if regional capacity is saturated, prefer degrade to a smaller-model variant in-region rather than cross-region failover; discuss canaries for multi-region rollout.

Attachments: I’m attaching a draft SLO matrix and a short network topology diagram for your infra team to review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Aditya will follow up with a short technical note on routing & cache behaviour and a sample perf run (see attachment).
2) We’ll schedule a POC deep-dive next week to validate p95 numbers with a representative prompt set and region-level load tests.
3) Finova to confirm whether EU residency requirement is strict (no processing in non-EU) or if pseudonymized/aggregated backup copies are acceptable.

Can you confirm the above and suggest 2x 60-minute windows next week for the POC? I’ve tentatively proposed Wed/Thu in the Calendly link below.

Thanks —

Hi Samira / team — following up with the technical context we discussed. Short answers first, details below.

1) Routing & residency: Redwood supports region-specific tenancy. For strict EU residency we can deploy a tenant in the EU region (data plane and KV caches stay in-region). Hosted EU tenancy is available; for additional isolation we can provision Dedicated EU capacity (reserved GPUs) which guarantees no cross-border processing.

2) Latency & throughput: in our benchmarks, a medium-sized chat model (7B) with optimized kernels and continuous batching typically achieves P95 token-generation latency of ~120–180ms in the same region under 100 concurrent streams. Larger models (13B+) trend higher (~180–280ms) depending on sequence length and batching. Streaming adds a small header cost but does not materially increase steady-state P95 for token delivery.

3) Concurrency and burst handling: We can meet your burst concurrency (120 simultaneous requests) via autoscaling policy + burst reserve. For predictable SLA-backed behavior we recommend Dedicated capacity for the EU region — it reduces variance and gives capacity guarantees.

4) Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming (server-sent events / chunked transfer). We expose a chunk-size and flush interval you can tune. For progressive render we recommend 200–300ms flush windows depending on UX.

5) Fallback strategy: We can configure a policy: (a) in-region smaller-model fallback (same region) -> (b) cross-region fallback only if in-region capacity is exhausted and EU residency rules allow it. We will add canary rollout policies for models and routing to avoid broad regressions.

Action items for POC:
- Finova: provide representative prompt set and a short list of pilot user regions (US/EU/APAC) + traceroute results from your infra to our EU endpoint.
- Redwood: we’ll run a 2-hour load test per region and share a perf-run HTML report (attached).
- Cost estimate: we need to size Dedicated capacity for your target concurrency; I’ll follow up with a ballpark delta by EOD.

Perf run attachment: perf-run-20260220.html (summary + trace artifacts).
